talib_customer: Hey team — seeing a few hundred 429s for ~3 minutes during our nightly CI backfill at 00:00 UTC. It looks like requests spike then quickly subside. Sample header from a failed request: `Retry-After: 8`, `X-Account-Id: acct_78xxx`, request-id `r-0a1b2c`. Any quick mitigation?
sara_support: Thanks Talib — sorry about that. Can you confirm whether these are parallel short requests (many small calls) or long streaming calls? Also which plan/account alias?
talib_customer: All small calls, ~40ms avg, we fan out across 300 workers at once to warm caches. Account is acct_78xxx on growth tier.
quota-bot: Alert: account acct_78xxx exceeded short-term burst allowance at 2551234559, 429s issued until cushion recovered.
sara_support: Looks like you exhausted the burst credit cushion. Short-lived spikes from parallel workers are exactly the pattern we throttle. Two immediate mitigations: 1) add client-side token bucket to cap peak concurrency, 2) enable request jitter/stagger in your backfill jobs. Can you share a minimal curl that reproduces the pattern?
talib_customer: Repro (simplified):
```
for i in {1..300}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
This produces a block of 429s for ~2-3 minutes, then all clears.
mike_infra: Confirming on infra side — we see a sharp dip in the per-account burst token bucket at 2551234560. Refill rate is 1 token/sec for this account's baseline; the bucket capacity is small (configured due to tier). When many short requests arrive simultaneously the tokens run out and the smoothing window kicks in.
sara_support: For short term: set client-side concurrency -> 50 workers (or gradual ramp) and add exponential backoff with jitter (start 100ms, max 5s). That eliminates the sudden drain.
talib_customer: Any server-side knobs we can flip so future backfills don't need heavy client changes?
mike_infra: Two server-side options: 1) request a temporary reserved cushion (we can grant a one-off "burst top-up" for a scheduled backfill), 2) tune the account smoothing window from 60s -> 300s which spreads refill across a longer window and reduces immediate 429s but increases steady tail latency risk. Both require engineering approval for permanent change.
sara_support: I can provision a one-time cushion for tonight's backfill. If you plan recurring hourly jobs we recommend either: - stagger start times, or - reduce parallelism per host + increase per-host queuing. We also recommend enabling our per-route prewarm cache to reduce calls.
talib_customer: Ok let's do the one-time cushion tonight, and we'll stagger next week. Can you also document the header that indicates remaining burst tokens? We only saw `Retry-After`.
mike_infra: We'll ask infra to add `X-Burst-Remaining` in the response headers for future visibility. For now, `Retry-After` + `429` is the signal. I'll put a short follow-up PR to console docs.
sara_support: Provisioned a temporary +12k token cushion for acct_78xxx for window 2551234560-2551240000. Please run your backfill and report. Also created support ticket #SUP-2026-332 to track tuning and docs updates. :white_check_mark:
talib_customer: Backfill ran — no 429s this time, great. Will implement stagger and client throttling next week. Thanks! :pray:
sara_support: Great — leaving this thread open until docs headers added. I'll follow up when `X-Burst-Remaining` lands.
mike_infra: Filed infra task INF-742: add `X-Burst-Remaining` and `X-Burst-Window` headers, and doc snippet for smoothing params. ETA ~3 business days.
sara_support: Closing notes for the ticket: reproduce with 300 parallel small requests -> 429 window ~2-3m; short-term mitigation = temporary cushion; long-term = stagger + client-side token-bucket; infra action = header visibility + docs.
talib_customer: Perfect, thanks everyone.
